translations.text: The proverbs of Solomon, son of David, who reigned over Israel in Jerusalem.
For knowing wisdom and discipline, and for understanding words of wisdom.
For receiving turns of speech and understanding true righteousness.
For directing judgment rightly, so as to give wisdom to the innocent, and discernment and understanding to children and young people.
When a wise person hears this, he will increase in wisdom.
Whoever has gained guidance will understand a proverb and a hidden saying, the sayings of the wise, in an instant.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and all who practice it have good understanding. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of discernment. The wicked despise wisdom and discipline.
Listen, my son, to your father's instruction, and do not reject your mother's command.
You will receive a glorious crown for your head and a golden necklace for your neck.
My son, do not let wicked people lead you astray, and do not agree if they urge you, saying, “Come, share in bloodshed with us.
And let us unjustly bury a righteous man in the ground.
Let us swallow him alive like hell and erase his memory from the earth.
Let us gather his abundant possessions and fill our houses with plunder.
Join us, and let us all have one purse and one bag.”
My son, do not travel along the road with them.
Keep your feet away from their tracks, for their feet run toward evil and hurry to shed blood.
For it is not in vain that they spread a snare for people.
Those who are accustomed to killing store up evil for themselves. The downfall of sinful people is terrible.
This is the way of all who commit sins. Sin and violence destroy their lives.
Wisdom is praised in the streets, and she raises her voice in the public squares.
She is proclaimed on the tops of the walls. She takes her place at the gates of the powerful, and at the city gates she speaks boldly.
As long as the innocent possess righteousness, they will not be ashamed.

How long, you wicked people, will you love error? Fools are lovers of mockery. Having become wicked, they hated understanding and became defiled before those who rebuke them. Why do you turn away my rebuke?
Look, I will tell you the breath of my words and teach you my sayings.
For I called, and you did not answer me. I stretched out my hands, and you did not listen to me.
I spoke at length, and you did not obey me. You treated my command as contemptible and paid no attention to my rebuke.
I too will laugh at your destruction and rejoice when the onslaught of ruin comes upon you.
And when destruction comes upon you [?], and devastation likewise, when it comes upon you to ensnare them, and when distress and persecution come upon you, I was there.
When you call on me, I in turn will not listen to you. Evil people will seek me but will not find me.
For they hated wisdom and did not want to hear the word of the Lord.
They did not want to consider my counsel, and they despised all my correction.
Then they will eat the fruit of their deeds and be filled with their own sins.
For the refusal of fools to turn back will kill them. Because they oppressed the little ones, they will be killed, and the examination of the wicked will kill them.
But whoever waits for me in hope will rest without fear of any evil.
My son, if you receive the words of my commandment and store them in your heart,
if you make your ear listen to wisdom, give your heart to understanding, and turn your heart toward instruction,
and if you call out for wisdom, raise your voice for understanding, and seek insight with great effort,
and if you seek it like silver and search for it like buried treasure,
then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
For the Lord gives wisdom, and from his presence come insight and understanding.
He stores up salvation for those who act rightly and stands guard over their paths as paths of righteousness. He preserves the path of those who fear him.
Then you will understand justice and righteousness and make good paths straight.
For if wisdom enters your mind and understanding becomes pleasing to your soul,
she will guard you with good counsel and shelter you with righteous understanding,
to save you from the evil path and from the man who speaks no sound word at all,
Woe to those who abandon straight paths to walk on paths of darkness.
and from those who rejoice in evil and delight in evil's perversity.
Their paths are contentious and their tracks are crooked, so that they may lead you away from the straight path and make you a stranger to the path of understanding righteousness.
My son, do not let evil counsel overtake you, the counsel that abandons the instruction of your youth.
My son, keep my words so that they may deliver you from an evil and foreign woman whose words are deceitful, who has abandoned the husband of her youth and forgotten the ordinance of God.
She has settled near death and near Sheol, and has directed her paths among the earthborn giants.
None of those who go to her return, nor do they find straight paths, nor will they be found in the years of life.
But if they walked on straight paths, they would find the smooth paths of righteousness. Those who live on the earth will be good, and the innocent will remain in it.
For the upright will inhabit the earth, and the righteous will remain in it.
The paths of the wicked will be wiped from the earth, and the lawless will be driven out of it.
My son, do not forget my law, and let your heart keep my words.
Length of days, years of life, and peace will be added to you.
Do not let charity and faithfulness depart. Bind them around your neck and write them on the tablet of your heart.
And you will find favor. Consider what is good in the sight of God and people.
Trust in God with all your heart, and do not pride yourself on your own wisdom.
Honor her in all your ways, so that she may make your paths straight.
Do not be wise in your own eyes, but fear God and turn away from all evil.
Then this will bring healing to your flesh and relief to your bones.
Honor God with the possessions you have acquired righteously, and bring him the first of your harvest and the fruit of your righteousness.
Then your storehouses will overflow with abundant wheat, and your vats will overflow with wine.
My son, do not despise God's discipline, and do not grow weary of him when he rebukes you.
For God disciplines the one he loves, like a father who delights in his son, and he whips all his children who do not accept it.
Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, and [?] the mortal who understands prudence.
Gaining her is better than gaining gold and silver and abundant treasures.
She is more precious than a pearl of great price, and nothing evil can stand against her.
She is a good city for all who approach her, and no honor is equal to her. Length of days and years of life are in her right hand.
In her left hand are honor and wealth. Righteous law comes from her mouth, and she clothes her tongue with mercy. Her paths are paths of life, and all her tracks are peaceful.
She is a tree of life to all who hold fast to her, and for those who trust in her, she is secure in God.
The Lord founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding.
By his knowledge the depths burst open, and the clouds pour down dew.
My son, do not be careless. Keep my counsel and my understanding, so that your soul may live.
They will be an ornament around your neck, healing for your flesh, and relief for your bones, so that you may walk confidently and peacefully in all your ways.
Your feet will not stumble. If you sit down, you will not be afraid.
If you lie down, you will sleep sweetly. Do not fear the sudden alarm that comes upon you, or the approaching terror of the wicked.
For God will be with you in all your ways, and he will keep your feet steady so that they do not slip.
Do not neglect to do good to the needy. Help him as much as it is in your power to do.
Do not say, "Go away and come back; I will give you something tomorrow," when you can do good now, for you do not know what the next day will bring.
Furthermore, do not plan evil against your friend who lives with you and trusts you. Do not seek to quarrel with anyone without cause, if he has done you no harm.
Do not acquire carelessness among evil people, lest you become like them.
Do not envy their ways, for every sinner is loathsome to God and does not associate with the righteous.
God's curse is in the houses of the wicked.
The Lord’s blessing is in the houses of the righteous, but wrath opposes the proud.
He gives honor to the humble, and the wise will inherit honor.
But the wicked have increased their disgrace.
Listen, my children, to a father’s instruction, so that the days of your life may be many.
Apply your minds to understanding, for I give you a good gift. Do not abandon my law.
For I too was a son who obeyed his father, and I was loved in my mother’s sight.
They taught me and said to me, “Let our words enter your heart. Keep our commandments.
Do not forget or disregard the words of our mouths, and do not abandon her.
Acquire understanding, and she will welcome you. Love her,
and she will guard you. Embrace her, and she will raise you up.”
Listen, my son, and receive my words, so that the years of your life may increase and the paths of your life may be many.
For I teach you the way of wisdom and establish you on straight tracks.
When you walk, your steps will not be hindered, and when you run, you will not grow weary. Accept my word; do not abandon it.
Keep her for yourself, and do not abandon her, for the sake of your life.
Do not walk in the way of the wicked, and do not envy the paths of sinners. Do not go to the place where they have gone. Withdraw from them and turn away.
For they do not sleep unless they have done evil; sleep is taken from their eyes.
They do not sleep unless they have done harm—those who eat the food of sin and get drunk on the wine of injustice.
But the path of the righteous shines like light. They go on and shine until the day is fully established.
But the path of sinners is darkness, and they do not know that they will stumble.
My son, pay attention to my words, and let your ear listen to what I say, so that your springs do not run dry.
Keep them in your heart, for they are life to those who find them and to the whole body.
With all vigilance, guard your heart from this path, for it is the fountain of life.
Keep an evil mouth far from you, and put unjust lips far away from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids glance toward what is right.
Make a straight track for your feet, and straighten your paths.
Do not turn aside to the right or to the left. Turn your feet away from the evil path, for the Lord loves the paths on the right.
The paths on the left are crooked, but he will make straight tracks for your feet and make your journey prosper in peace.
My son, pay attention to my wisdom, and let your ear listen to my words, so that she may guard you with good judgment.
And learn from my lips what I command you.
Do not look at an evil woman, for honey flows from the lips of an adulterous woman, sweetening your throat for a time.
But afterward you will find something more bitter than gall and sharper than a double-edged sword.
Her feet lead down toward folly, and her steps lead into death and the underworld.
Her tracks do not leave the place of sin or approach the paths of life. Her courses are slippery and cannot be known.
And now, my son, listen to me, and do not despise my words.
Keep your path far from her, and do not approach the door of her house,
so that you do not give your life to another and your livelihood to those who have no mercy,
so that strangers do not feast on your strength, and the fruit of your labor does not enter another's house.
Then you will regret it afterward, when the flesh of your body has wasted away.
And you will say, “How I hated instruction from my youth, and my ear turned away from correction!”
I did not listen to the words of those who taught and corrected me, nor did I pay attention with my ears.
I came close to falling into every kind of evil.

In the midst of the assembly and the congregation. Drink water from your own cistern and from the spring of your own well. Let waters flow from your well, and let your waters run through your public squares.
Let them be yours alone, with no stranger sharing them with you, and let your well of water be your own.
Rejoice with the wife of your youth.
With the love of a deer and a fawn, love your wife.
May the charm of her love satisfy you. Let her be your own, and let her remain with you at all times.
As you love one another with this love, you will grow in number, and all you have will not belong to a strange woman.
Do not stretch out your hand toward a woman who is not yours.
For a man's paths are before the eyes of the Lord, and he examines all his courses.
Sin ensnares a person, and everyone is entangled in the cord of sin.
This man will die with fools. Through his great folly his life is lost, and he is destroyed because of his foolishness.
My son, if you have become a guarantor for your friend, you give your hand to an enemy.
A strong snare lies in a man's lips, and he is destroyed by the lips of his own mouth.
My son, do what I command you, and save yourself. For if you have fallen into the hands of wicked people because of your friend, do not be idle, but press the friend for whom you have given a pledge,
Do not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids.
so that you may escape like a gazelle from a snare and like a bird from a trap.
Turn to the ant, you idler, and do not be idle. Observe its ways, imitate them, and become wise through it.
Though it has no field and no one to compel it to work, and though it has no master, it gathers abundant food in summer and works at harvest time to lay up supplies.

Or go to the bee and learn how industrious she is and how well she does her work. Kings and fools take the fruit of her labor for sustenance. She is desired by everyone and is honored. Though weak in strength, she is strong in her work.
By honoring wisdom, she has gained recognition. How long will you lie there, sluggard? When will you wake from your sleep?
You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, and fold your hands on your back a little.
Then destitution will come upon you like an evil traveler, and poverty and hardship like a good runner.
But if you are not lazy, your harvest will come to you like a spring, and poverty itself will flee far from you like an evil runner.
A foolish and lawless man walks in ways that are not good. He winks with his eye, signals with his foot, and makes signs with his fingers.
A rebellious heart plans evil at all times. Such a person brings turmoil upon a city.
Therefore destruction will come upon him suddenly—a blow and a crushing from which he will not recover.
For he rejoices in everything the Lord hates, and he will be crushed because of the impurity of his soul.
There are six things that the Lord hates, and the seventh is abhorrent to his soul:
arrogant eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed the blood of the righteous;
a heart that produces evil thoughts, and feet that hurry to do evil;
and one who stirs up false testimony and spreads conflict among brothers.
My son, keep your father's laws, and do not reject your mother's commandment.
Put it in your heart at all times, and bind it around your neck.
When you walk, take it with you, and it will remain with you. When you sleep, it will guard you, and when you rise, it will speak to you.
For the commandment is a lamp, the law is light, and correction and instruction are the path of life.
My son, keep my commandment so that it may protect you from another man's wife and from the flattery of an evil tongue.
Do not let her alluring beauty overcome you. Do not be ensnared by her eyes or captivated by her eyelids.
The love of a prostitute costs a single loaf of bread, but a woman [?] destroys the lives of the honorable and ensnares them.
Who can gather fire into his lap without his clothes being burned?
And who can walk on burning coals without his feet being burned?
So it is with the man who enters the house of another man's wife: he will not be innocent, nor will anyone who touches her.
It is no wonder if a thief is caught stealing, for he steals to satisfy his hunger.
But if he is caught, he must repay sevenfold and give all his possessions to save his life.
But an adulterer, through lack of understanding, brings destruction upon his own life.
He brings suffering and disgrace upon himself, and his dishonor will never be erased.
For the husband is full of jealousy and anger, and he will show him no mercy on the day of judgment.
He will not exchange his hatred for any ransom, nor will he be reconciled by many gifts.
My son, keep my words, and let my commandment come to you.
My son, honor the Lord, and you will be stronger than all. Apart from him, fear no other, for there is no one who can kill you and no one who can give you life.
My son, keep my commandment and live; keep my words like the pupil of your eye.
Put it on your fingers and write it on the broad surface of your heart.
Say to wisdom, “You are my sister,” and make understanding your kinswoman.
So that it may protect you from a strange and wicked woman and from the deceitful words she brings to you.
For she looks out from the window of her house into the streets.
If she sees among the foolish youths a young man lacking understanding, walking along the streets near the corner of her house, (she calls him and says to him).
And he speaks in the darkness of evening, when there is silence and the darkness of night.
Then she confronts him, dressed like a prostitute, a woman who makes young men’s hearts flutter.
She is restless, married, and dissolute, and her feet do not stay at home.
Sometimes she wanders outside, and sometimes she waits in the streets and at the corners.
She takes hold of him and kisses him, and shamelessly says to his face:
“I have a peace offering; [?] I am fulfilling my vows.
For this very reason I came out to meet you, and longing to see your face, I found you.
I have covered my bed with fine linen and spread rugs from Egypt. I have sprinkled my bed with saffron and my house with cinnamon. Come, let us delight in kisses until morning.
Let us revel in love, for my husband is not at home.
He has gone to a distant country, taking a store of gold in his hand, and it will be many days before he returns home.”
She led him astray with many words and drew him in with the snare of her lips.
He follows her submissively, like an ox going to slaughter and like a dog going to be bound.
And like a stag that has been pierced and whose liver has been wounded, he rushes like a bird into a snare.
He does not know that his rush will cost him his life.
And now, my son, listen to me and pay attention to the words of my mouth.
Do not let your [?] turn toward her paths, and do not stray in her tracks.
She has led many astray and wounded them, and those she has led astray cannot be counted.
Her house is a road to Sheol, leading down into the chambers of death.
But you, proclaim wisdom, so that understanding may answer you.
For she is on the highest heights and stands in the middle of the roads, and she waits at the gates of the powerful.
In the streets she is praised: “To you, people, I appeal, and I speak my word to humankind.
You who are simple, learn prudence, and you fools, acquire understanding.
Listen to me, for I make things clear, and I bring forth what is right from my lips.
For my throat teaches righteousness, and lying lips are an abomination to me.
All the words of my mouth are righteous; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.
They are all straightforward to those who understand, and right to those who find insight.
Choose instruction rather than silver, and knowledge rather than tested gold, and receive discernment rather than pure gold.
For wisdom is better than a costly pearl, and nothing precious can compare with her.
I, Wisdom, have dwelt with counsel, and I have summoned knowledge and understanding.
Whoever fears the Lord hates injustice. I hate hatred, arrogance, and evil ways.
I also hate the crooked paths of the wicked. Counsel and authority are mine; understanding is mine, and strength is mine.
Through me kings reign, and rulers write just decrees.
Through me great men gain honor, and princes hold the land.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me find favor.
Honor and wealth are with me, and abundant possessions. Righteousness is better; choose it over gold and precious pearls.
My fruit is better than pure silver.
I walk in the paths of righteousness and travel along the tracks of justice,
so that I may distribute wealth to those who know me and fill their storehouses with abundance.
If I have told you what will happen tomorrow, I will also recall and recount what has been from eternity.
The Lord created me before all his works, before he established the world,
before he made the earth, before he made the depths, and before the springs of water came forth.
Before the mountains were planted (established), and before the hills, he gave birth to me.
And before he made [?] and the inhabited ends beneath heaven.
When he prepared the heavens, I was there, and when he established his throne upon the winds,
and when he made the clouds above firm, and when he firmly established the springs of water,
and when he set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not go beyond his command,
and when he made the foundations of the earth firm, I was with him, putting things in order.
I was the one who rejoiced each morning and delighted in his presence at all times, and when he rejoiced after completing the world. My delight was in human beings.
And now, my son, listen to me. Blessed are those who keep my ways.
Listen to wisdom and become wise, and do not give up. Blessed is the person who listens to my words.
Blessed is the one who keeps my ways, stays watchful at my gates each morning, and guards the doorposts of my entrance.
For my paths are paths of life. Whoever finds me finds life, and his desire will be acceptable to the Lord.
But those who sin against me wrong themselves, and those who hate me love death.
Wisdom built herself a house and set up seven pillars.
She slaughtered her animals and added wine to her mixing bowl.
She sent out her servants, calling with a loud proclamation,
saying, “Let whoever is foolish turn aside to me.” And to those who lack understanding
she said, “Come, eat my bread and drink my wine, which I have poured out for you.
Abandon foolishness and seek understanding, so that you may live.”
Set your understanding right through inquiry. Whoever instructs evil people brings disgrace upon himself.
Whoever rebukes a wicked person harms himself.
Do not rebuke fools, lest they hate you.
Rebuke a wise person, and he will love you, but a fool will hate you. Give a wise person instruction, and he will increase in wisdom. Teach a wise person, and he will accept still more.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of holy people is understanding. Knowledge of the law is good for the heart.
By this discipline you will live many days, and years of life will be added to you.
My son, if you become wise, you will be wise for yourself and for your neighbor; but if you become evil, you alone will draw out evil for yourself.
Whoever prepares falsehood is like someone preparing winds; he is like someone pursuing a flying bird.

He has abandoned the paths of his vineyard and forgotten his wheels and his fruit. He wanders into a barren wilderness and into a land appointed for thirst, and with his hands he gathers what neither bears fruit nor sprouts.
A foolish, domineering woman is in need of bread. She knows no shame at all, and she sits at the entrance of her house.
On her seat, openly in the square, she calls to those passing along the road, who are going straight on their way.
Whoever among them is foolish, let him approach her; and she addresses the one who lacks understanding.
She says to him, “Eat the hidden bread I have kept for you, and drink stolen water with pleasure.”
But he does not know that mighty men perish beside her, and that the depths of Sheol are found in her house.
But leap away, and do not linger in her place. Do not keep your eyes fixed on her, so that you may pass beyond a foreign river.
Keep far from foreign water, and do not drink from a foreign well, so that you may live many days and years of life may be added to you.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son grieves his mother.
Treasures do not benefit sinners, but righteousness saves from death.
The Lord does not let a righteous soul go hungry, but he uproots the lives of the wicked from the earth.
An idle hand brings a person low, but a diligent hand makes a person rich.
An instructed son becomes wise, but a fool makes himself a servant. A wise son escapes scorching heat.
A wise son works at harvest, but a foolish son sleeps at harvest. A sinful son becomes a taker of life on the threshing floor.
The Lord’s blessing is upon the heads of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked brings [?] to completion.
The memory of the righteous is accompanied by praise, but the name of the wicked will perish.
A wise heart accepts commandments, but whoever does not restrain his lips falls into a snare.
Whoever walks with integrity walks securely, but whoever makes his ways crooked will be exposed.
Whoever winks his eyes for evil brings sorrow upon people, but whoever rebukes openly makes peace.
A fountain of life is in the mouths of the righteous, but destruction covers the mouths of the wicked.
Hatred stirs up wrath, but love covers all who transgress.
A wise man brings wisdom from his lips; a man without sense strikes with a rod (is struck with a rod).
A wise person stores up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool comes close to destruction.
The wealth of the rich is a fortified city, but the destruction of the wicked is their poverty of knowledge.
The work of the righteous produces life, but the fruit of the wicked is sin.
Discipline guards the paths of life; whoever does not persist in discipline goes astray.
Flattering lips conceal hatred, and those who spread slander are fools.
Through much talking a sinner does not escape sin, but whoever restrains his lips becomes wise.
The tongue of a righteous person is refined silver, but the heart of the wicked is worth little.
The lips of the righteous know great things, but fools die for lack of understanding.
The blessing of the Lord is upon the heads of the righteous; it makes them rich and brings no sorrow into the heart.
The wicked person returns to destruction; the righteous person's desire finds favor with the Lord.
When the storm passes, the wicked person perishes, but the righteous person, through correction, will be saved forever.
As sour grapes are bad for the teeth and smoke for the eyes, so sin is for those who acquire it.
Fear of the Lord lengthens one's days, but the years of the wicked will be shortened.
Joy takes root among the righteous, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
The fear of the Lord is strength for the good person, but destruction for those who do evil.
The righteous person will never stumble, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.
The mouth of the righteous speaks wisdom, but the tongue of the unjust will be destroyed.
The lips of the righteous pour forth grace, but the mouth of the wicked is cut off from understanding.
The plans of the unjust are abominable to God, but the plans of the righteous are approved.
Where there is slander, there is disgrace, but the mouth of the humble learns wisdom.
The integrity of the righteous guides them, but the perversity of the wicked destroys them.

Wealth is of no use on the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death. When a righteous person dies, he leaves regret; [?] will be at hand, and the death of the wicked will be a cause for laughter.
The righteousness of the innocent makes his path straight, but sin comes down upon the wicked.
The righteousness of upright people delivers them, but sinners are caught through their ignorance.
When a righteous man dies, his hope does not perish, but the confidence of the wicked disappears.
The righteous person escapes from distress, and a wicked person is given in exchange for him.
In the mouth of the wicked is a trap for the city, but recognizing righteousness is a good path.
Through the goodness of the righteous a city prospers, and at the destruction of the wicked it rejoices.
Through the blessing of the upright a city is exalted, but through the mouths of the wicked it is overthrown.
The people of a city despise a poor wise man, but a wise man brings silence.
A double-tongued man reveals the deliberations of an assembly, but one who is trustworthy in spirit conceals a matter.
Those who have no guide fall like leaves, but deliverance comes through much counsel.
A wicked man does evil when he associates with a righteous man, and he hates the sound of protection.
A good wife brings honor to her husband, but a wife who hates righteousness is a seat of disgrace.
The lazy become poor instead of wealthy, but the diligent accumulate wealth.
A merciful man does good to himself, but one who shows no mercy ruins his own body.
A wicked man does unjust deeds, but a reward awaits the offspring of the righteous.
A righteous son is born for life, but the offspring of the wicked are born for death.
Crooked paths are unclean before the Lord, but all who are pure in their ways are favored in his sight.
One who joins hand in hand with violence will not escape sin, but one who sows righteousness will receive the reward of the faithful.
Like a gold ornament in the tip of a foul pig’s snout is beauty in an evil woman.
The path of righteousness is entirely good, but the hope of the wicked perishes.
Some scatter what they own and gain more, while others gather and have less.
Every soul that is blessed is generous, but an angry man [?].
Whoever hoards his grain leaves it to the nations, and the poor curse him; but blessing rests on the head of the one who shows mercy and gives.
Whoever plans good seeks a good reputation, but whoever searches for evil will be found by it.
Whoever trusts in his wealth will fall, but whoever welcomes the righteous will be established.
Whoever neglects his household will inherit the wind, and a fool will serve a wise man.
From the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life, and the lives of the unjust are snatched away [?].
If the righteous man is saved only with difficulty, where will the wicked man, the sinner, and the unjust appear?
Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is a fool.
Better is the one who has found favor with the Lord, but an unjust man will be condemned.
A person who is not upright will be destroyed through injustice, but the root of the righteous will not be uprooted.
An obedient wife is a crown to her husband. As a worm is to wood, so a wife of wicked conduct destroys a man's heart.
The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the wicked devise deceit.
The speech of the wicked is treachery, but the mouth of the wicked saves them.
Wherever the wicked man turns, he perishes, but the houses of the righteous remain.
A wise person's mouth is praised by everyone, but a corrupt heart is despised.
Better a man who serves in a lowly position than one who gives himself honor but lacks bread.
A righteous man has compassion on the life of his animal, but the mercy of the wicked is no kindness.
Whoever cultivates the land increases his bread, but whoever pursues worthless things gathers poverty, because he lacks understanding.
The man who delights in pursuing wine leaves disgrace in his stronghold.
The desire of the wicked is evil, but the roots of the good are firmly established.
Through the sin of his lips, a sinner falls into a trap, but a righteous man escapes from it.
Whoever looks kindly will be shown mercy, but whoever fights at the gates brings distress to people.
From the fruit of his mouth, a man's soul is filled with blessing, and the reward of his lips is given to him.
The path of fools is right in their own eyes, but the ear of the wise listens to counsel.
A fool declares his anger at daybreak, but a sensible man conceals his disgrace.
A righteous man speaks what reveals faithfulness, but the testimony of the wicked is deceit.
Those who bear false witness kill with a sword, for a sword lies in their mouths; but the tongue of the wise heals the wounded.
The lips of the righteous establish testimony, but a hasty witness has an evil tongue.
Deceit is in the heart of anyone who plans evil, but those who desire peace rejoice.
Nothing evil pleases the righteous, but the wicked multiply evil.
Lying lips are detestable to the Lord, but whoever acts faithfully is pleasing to him.
A sensible man is a throne of wisdom, but the heart of fools encounters a curse.
The hand of the chosen will quickly take control, but the deceitful will become plunder.
An alarming word troubles the heart of a righteous man, but good news gladdens the heart of a wise man.
A righteous man understands himself, but the nature of the wicked is not human.
Evil pursues those who sin, and the path of the wicked leads them astray.
A deceitful man fails in his hunting, but a pure man is a precious possession.
There is life in the paths of righteousness, but those who remember evil remain in death.
A sensible son listens to his father, but a son who does not listen comes to destruction.
A good man eats from the fruit of his righteousness, but the lives of the lawless perish before their time.
Whoever guards his mouth protects his life, but whoever is rash with his lips brings himself down.
Everyone who does not work lives in longing, but the hands of good people labor diligently.
The speech of an unjust man hates righteousness, but a wicked man is ashamed and does not appear openly.
Righteousness guards the innocent on their path, but sin makes the wicked worthless.
Some exalt themselves although they have nothing, and some humble themselves although their wealth is great.
A man's wealth is the ransom for his life, but a poor man cannot withstand wrath.
There is light for the righteous at all times, but the light of the wicked will go out.
Deceitful souls go astray in sin, but the righteous show mercy and give alms.
An evil person acts wickedly in his arrogance, but those who know themselves are wise.
Wealth amassed through sin will dwindle in the end, but whoever gathers for himself in righteousness will have an abundance. The righteous person also shows mercy and lends.
One who begins to help himself is better than one who becomes rich and relies on hope.
The good path is a tree of life.
Whoever despises the work of God will himself be despised by God, but whoever fears his commandment will live by it.
Nothing good comes to a deceitful son, but a wise servant’s work will prosper, and his path will be straight.
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, but whoever lacks understanding dies in sin.
Good understanding gives wisdom and favor, but the paths of the wicked lead to destruction.
Every discerning person acts with counsel, but a fool displays his wickedness.
A foolish messenger falls into trouble, but a wise envoy saves himself.
Instruction removes poverty and disgrace, and whoever heeds correction will be honored.
The desire of good people brings healing to the soul, but the conduct of the wicked is far from understanding.
Whoever associates with a wise person becomes wise, but whoever wanders about with fools becomes a fool.
Evil pursues those who do wrong, but good comes to the righteous.
A good man sees his children’s children, and the wealth of the wicked is stored up for the righteous.
The righteous live in wealth for many years, but the unjust perish quickly.
Whoever withholds his rod hates his son, but whoever loves his son disciplines him continually.
The righteous person eats and satisfies his appetite, but the wicked go hungry.
Wise women build houses, but foolish women tear down their houses with their own hands.
Whoever walks a straight path fears God, but whoever makes his path crooked will be despised.
From the mouths of fools comes a rod of arrogance, but the lips of the wise protect them.
Where there are no oxen, the feeding trough is clean, but where grain is abundant, it is recognized as the result of the ox’s strength.
The testimony of the faithful does not lie, and it sets the soul of a false witness on fire.
You will seek wisdom among the wicked and will not find it, but understanding is easy for the wise.
Everything seems right to a foolish man, but the lips of the wise are a shield of knowledge.
The wisdom of discerning people knows their path, but the path of those without understanding leads into error.
The households of sinners will make restitution to the innocent, but the households of the righteous are acceptable.
A person’s heart knows the sorrow of his own soul, and when it rejoices, hatred does not mingle with it.
The houses of the wicked will be ruined, but the dwelling of the upright will stand.
There is a path that seems right to people, but in the end it leads to the depths of Sheol.
Sorrow is not mixed into joy, but the end of joy turns to grief.
The proud in heart will be filled with the fruits of their own ways, but a good man will be filled with blessing from his own intentions.
The simple person believes every word, but the discerning person turns to reflection.
The wise person fears and withdraws from evil, but the fool trusts in himself and joins with fools.
An angry person acts without counsel, but a wise person shows great patience.
Fools share in evil, but discerning people take hold of knowledge.
Evil people stumble before the good, and the wicked become servants at the gates of the righteous.
The friends of the rich hate the friends of the poor, and the rich have many friends.
Whoever despises the poor will become poor, but whoever has mercy on the needy is blessed.
Those who go astray devise evil, but good people devise kindness and righteousness. Those who practice evil do not know kindness or mercy.
But mercy and faithfulness are with those who do good. There is profit in all planning, but the idle person who takes no trouble is needy.
The crown of the wise is knowledge, but the teacher of fools is evil.
A discerning witness saves his life from evil, but a deceitful witness kindles a fire with lies.
In the fear of God there is strong confidence, and he leaves a stronghold for his children.
The commandment of the Lord is a spring of life, and it enables people to escape the snares of death.
A king’s glory lies in a multitude of people, but a ruler’s downfall lies in the scarcity of people.
A patient and understanding man will be wise.
A patient person becomes very wise, but an impatient person is a miserable fool.
A gentle person heals the heart. Jealousy is like rot to the bones, and arrogance is harmful to an understanding heart.
Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker, but whoever honors him shows mercy to the poor.
The wicked person is entangled in his own evil, but whoever trusts in his goodness is righteous.
Wisdom rests in the heart of a good person, but it is not known in the heart of a fool.
Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin diminishes a nation.
A discerning servant pleases the king, and through his carefulness he keeps disgrace away from himself. But anger destroys the wise.
Speaking humbly turns away wrath, but a hurtful word stirs up anger.
The heart of the wise knows what is good, but the mouths of fools proclaim evil.
The eyes of God are everywhere, and he watches the evil and the good.
A healing tongue is a tree of life, and whoever guards it will be filled with spirit.
A foolish son despises his father’s correction, but whoever heeds correction is wise.
Where righteousness abounds, there is great strength, but the wicked will be uprooted from the earth, roots and all.
The lips of the wise are restrained by knowledge, but the hearts of fools are not steadfast.
The sacrifice of the wicked is unclean before the Lord, but the prayer of the good is pleasing to him.
The way of the wicked is unclean before the Lord, but the Lord loves those who pursue righteousness.
The instruction of the innocent is recognized by passersby, but those who hate rebuke will die a wretched death.
Gehenna and death lie exposed before the Lord; how much more the human heart!
A fool does not love those who correct him and does not converse with the wise.
When the heart rejoices, it brightens the face; but when it grieves, it darkens it.
An upright heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of fools seeks evil all the time.
The eyes of the wicked long for evil, but the good are at peace at all times.
A small portion with fear of the Lord is better than great treasures without fear of him.
A meal of vegetables with love is better than a fattened ox with hatred.
An angry man stirs up a quarrel, but a patient man puts it out even after it has begun. A wicked man greatly increases hostility.
The paths of the lazy are strewn with thorns, but those of the diligent are smooth.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son despises his mother.
The paths of a fool who lacks knowledge are crooked, but a wise man walks straight.
Those who honor the assembly gain understanding, and counsel dwells in the hearts of counselors.
An evil person will not listen to it, and there is no one who says anything pleasant and good to the assembly.
The thoughts of the wise are the path of life, so that he may turn aside and escape from Sheol.
The Lord tears down the houses of the arrogant, but he makes the widow's boundary secure.
Thoughts of injustice are despised by the Lord, but the words of the pure are pleasant.
Whoever accepts bribes destroys himself, but whoever hates accepting bribes will be saved.
Through charity and faithfulness sin is forgiven, and through fear of the Lord all evil is avoided.
The heart of the righteous learns faithfulness, but the mouth of the wicked speaks evil things.
The paths of righteous people are pleasing to the Lord, and for their sake even enemies become friends.
The Lord is far away from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous. A little bread with righteousness is better than abundant produce with injustice.
A good man's heart considers righteousness, so that the Lord may direct his steps. An eye that sees good things gladdens the heart, and good news refreshes my bones.
Whoever listens to a wise person's rebuke will be counted among the wise.
Whoever refuses correction hates himself, but whoever loves correction loves himself.
The fear of the Lord is good understanding, and wisdom is foremost and honorable to whoever responds to it; honor follows the humble.
Everything the humble person does is pleasing to the Lord, but the wicked will perish on an evil day.
A proud heart is unclean before the Lord; whoever joins hands in wrongdoing will not be acquitted.
The beginning of a good path is doing what is right; this is much more pleasing to the Lord than slaughtering a sacrifice.
Whoever seeks the Lord will find knowledge through righteousness.
But those who seek what is right will find peace.
All the Lord's works are done with righteousness.
The wicked person is kept for an evil day.
An oracle is in a king's mouth, and his mouth does not err in judgment.
The Lord's judgment is like the tongue of a balanced scale, and his works are the weights of the balance.
An unjust balance is detestable to the Lord, and someone who does evil is detestable to a king. The throne of rulers stands firm through righteousness.
Righteous lips please a king, and the Lord loves upright speech.
A king's anger is like a messenger of death, but a wise person will appease him.
A king's face is like the light of the sun, but to those who displease him it is like an evening cloud.
Acquiring wisdom is worth more than gold, and acquiring understanding is better than silver.
The paths of life turn away from evil, and the paths of righteousness lead to a long life.
Whoever accepts instruction will prosper, and whoever heeds correction will become wise.
His ways safeguard his soul, and whoever loves his life guards his mouth.
Pride comes before conflict, and an evil mind comes before a fall.
Someone who humbly calms anger is better than someone who shares plunder with the proud.
Someone who acts with understanding finds good things, and whoever trusts in the Lord is blessed.
They call a wise person discerning, and they call someone whose speech is pleasant greater still.
Good sense is a fountain of life to those who possess it, but the instruction of fools is evil.
A wise person's heart is known from his mouth, and he carries understanding on his lips.
Good words are a honeycomb, and their sweetness heals the soul.
There are paths that seem right to a person, but their ends face the depths of Sheol.
A man toils for himself in his labor and forces ruin upon himself, but a crooked man carries ruin in his mouth.
A foolish man digs up evil for himself and stores fire in his lips.
A crooked man sends out evil, and the torch of deceit sets the wicked ablaze and separates friends.
An evil man deceives his friends and leads them along paths that are not good.
Someone who fixes his eyes intently plots deceit, and with his lips he determines every evil. He is a furnace of wickedness.
Gray hair is a beautiful crown of honor, and it is found on the paths of righteousness.
A patient man is better than a mighty man, and a man who has wisdom is better than great wealth.
One who rules his spirit is better than one who rules a city, and one who restrains his anger is better than one who conquers a city.
All the wrongdoing of an unjust man falls into his own lap, but everything righteous comes from the Lord.
A sweet morsel with peace is better than a house filled with many good things, or an unjust slaughter with strife.
A wise servant will rule over foolish masters and share the inheritance with the brothers.
As gold and silver are tested in a furnace, so chosen hearts are tested before the Lord.
The tongues of the lawless speak evil, but a righteous person pays no attention to lying lips.
For the faithful person, everything in the world is his wealth; but the unfaithful person does not have even a small coin.
Whoever mocks the poor provokes their Maker, and whoever rejoices over someone being ruined will not escape. But whoever shows mercy will receive mercy.
Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, and fathers are the pride of their children.
Trustworthy lips do not suit a fool, nor do lying lips suit a righteous person.
Instruction is a reward of favor to those who acquire it; wherever it turns, it makes its path beautiful.
Whoever conceals his offense seeks reconciliation, but whoever hates concealment separates friends and members of a household.
Pride grieves a wise heart, but a fool, even when beaten, does not understand his punishment.
Every evildoer raises a bow, and God sends his angel against him without mercy.
An understanding man falls into sorrow, but fools think about evil.
Whoever repays good with evil will never have evil depart from his house.
The shutting off of water is the beginning of hostility, and strife and fighting lead to poverty. The beginning of righteousness gives authority to speech.
Whoever judges a sinner as righteous, or a righteous person as a sinner, is unclean and despised before the Lord.
Why does a fool have wealth? Acquiring wisdom without understanding is impossible.
Whoever builds his house high seeks destruction for himself, and whoever resists instruction will fall into trouble.
At all times gain a friend, and let brothers be helpers in trouble, for this is why they are born.
A foolish man claps his hands and congratulates himself, like someone who boasts of a gift to his friend.
A lover of strife rejoices in fighting, but a hard-hearted person will encounter no good.
A man with a deceitful tongue falls into trouble, and a foolish heart brings sorrow to the one who possesses it.
A father does not rejoice in an undisciplined son, but a wise son makes his mother glad.
A joyful heart does good, but a sorrowful man dries up his bones.
Whoever unjustly receives gifts into his lap does not make justice straight, and the wicked person turns away from the paths of the righteous.
A wise man's face shows understanding, but a fool's eyes are at the ends of the earth. The wise man's eyes are in his head.
A foolish child brings anger to his father and sorrow to the woman who bore him.
It is not good to disgrace a righteous man, nor is it good to plot against righteous rulers.
Whoever holds back from uttering a harsh word is discerning, and a patient man is wise.
If a fool asks for wisdom, he will have it; through silence and self-restraint he will seem wise.
A man who wants to separate himself from his friends looks for an excuse, and he will always be a reproach.
Someone who lacks understanding does not desire wisdom; only folly rules him.
When a wicked person reaches the depths of evil, he becomes contemptuous and brings disgrace and reproach.
There is deep water in the heart of a wise person, and a flowing stream, a spring of life.
It is not good to show favoritism to the wicked, nor is it pleasing to deny justice in judgment.
A fool’s lips bring him into trouble, and an insolent person’s mouth calls down death on himself.
A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a trap for his life.
Lazy people increase fear, and the spirits of soft-living people go hungry.
Someone who does not sustain himself through his work is a brother to someone who devours himself.
The name of the Lord is a mighty strength, and by taking refuge in him the righteous are raised up.
A rich man’s wealth is a fortified city, and in its splendor it gives ample shelter.
Before destruction a person’s heart grows proud, and before honor it becomes humble.
Someone who speaks before listening is a fool and deserves contempt.
A wise servant calms a king’s anger, but who can endure a fainthearted man?
The heart of a wise person acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks words of instruction.
A gift raises a person up and seats him among rulers.
A righteous person accuses himself at the beginning of a case, and he rebuts what his opponent brings forward.
The lot puts an end to disputes and decides between the powerful.
A quiet person puts an end to disputes and settles matters among rulers.
A brother who helps his brother is like a strong, lofty city, and is as secure as a firmly rooted foundation.
A person fills his stomach with the fruit of his mouth and is satisfied with the fruit of his lips.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who master it will eat its fruit.
Whoever finds a good wife finds favor and receives kindness from the Lord.
Whoever sends away a good wife sends away good things, and whoever keeps an adulterous wife is foolish and wicked.
A person’s foolishness ruins his ways, and in his heart he blames the Lord.
A rich person gains many friends, but a poor person loses even the one he has.
A false witness is unclean, and whoever pursues violence will not escape.
Many serve before kings, but a person’s righteousness and wealth come only from the Lord.
And every evil becomes [?]. Every man who hates poor brothers is far from brotherhood with them.
Good understanding draws near to those who acquire it, and a wise man finds it.
Someone whose wickedness is great carries out evil, and someone who stirs up strife will not escape.
Whoever acquires wisdom loves his own soul, and whoever loves understanding will find good.
A false witness will not escape judgment, and whoever kindles evil will perish by it.
Luxury is not fitting for a fool; and if a servant exercises authority, it grows strong through arrogance.
A merciful man is patient, and he takes pride in his mercy by standing against sinners.
A king's anger is like a lion's roar, but his kindness is like dew falling on grass.
A foolish son is a disgrace to his father, and prayer offered with a prostitute's earnings is not pure.
Fathers divide houses and possessions among their children, but it is from the Lord that a wife comes to love her husband.
Fear seizes an effeminate man, and a person who does not work goes hungry.
Whoever keeps correction and the commandment safeguards his soul, but whoever neglects his ways will perish.
Whoever shows mercy to the poor lends to the Lord, and he will repay him according to what he has given.
Beat your son so that he may be a hope to you, but do not raise your hand against him in hostility.
An evil man destroys much, and if he is very arrogant, he adds his own life as well.
My son, listen to your father's correction, so that you may be wise in your later days.
There are many plans in the heart of a man who gives counsel, but the Lord's counsel remains forever.
A man's fruit is charity. A righteous poor man is better than a rich liar.
The fear of the Lord is a man's life, but someone who does not fear him lives in a place where understanding is not seen.
A lazy man hides his hand in his bosom and does not bring it to his mouth.
When an arrogant man is flogged, a fool becomes wise; and if you rebuke a wise man, he will reflect on understanding.
Whoever dishonors his father and mother will be excluded, put to shame, and despised.
A son who refuses to keep his father's instruction will learn evil speech.
Whoever stands surety for a foolish son treats justice with contempt, and evil judgment swallows up the wicked.
Flogging awaits the wicked, and judgment likewise awaits fools.
Wine is harmful to the beggar and the drunkard, and anyone who gives himself over to the cup is not wise. Every fool becomes entangled in this way.
A king's anger is no less than a lion's anger, and whoever provokes him wrongs his own soul.
It is a man's honor to refrain from strife, but every fool becomes entangled in such things.
Though people rebuke him, the lazy man feels no shame. He begs at harvest, but no one gives him anything, like someone who borrows wheat while he has it in his own heap.
Counsel in a person's heart is deep water, but a wise person draws it out.
A generous man is great and honorable, but finding a faithful man takes effort.
Whoever walks blamelessly in the law of the Lord makes his children blessed.
When a righteous king sits on his throne, nothing evil can stand before his eyes.
Who can boast that he has a pure heart? Who can show himself to be clean from sin?
Whoever reviles his father and mother will have his light extinguished, and his eyes will look upon darkness.
An inheritance acquired hastily at the beginning will not be blessed in the end.
Do not say, “I will take revenge on my enemies.” Instead, wait for the Lord to help you.
Large and small weights, and differing measures, are all detestable to the Lord. Whoever makes them will be ensnared by his own deeds.
The path of a righteous young man is straight.
The ear that hears and the eye that sees are both the work of the Lord.
Do not love slander, lest you [?], and do not sleep, lest you become poor. Open your eyes and have your fill of bread.
Both measures are despised by the Lord; a dishonest balance is not good in his sight.
A person's steps are directed by the Lord. How, then, can a mortal understand his own ways?
It is a snare for a person to hastily consecrate what belongs to him, for after making a vow he regrets it.
A wise king winnows the wicked and brings a wheel over them.
A person's breath is the light of the Lord.
Just as a lamp searches storehouses, so a wise king searches the storehouses of the belly.
A king preserves mercy and righteousness, and they sustain his throne in righteousness.
Wisdom is the adornment of the young, and gray hair is the honor of the old.
Blows and wounds crush the wicked, and beatings reach the innermost parts of the belly.
Like a stream of water, so is the king's heart in the Lord's hand. He turns it wherever he wishes, and there it goes.
Everyone appears righteous to himself, but the Lord sets hearts right.
Doing righteousness is enduring and pleasing to the Lord, more than slaughtering sacrifices.
A proud mind; a heart that does not [?] arrogance; the lamp of the wicked is sin.
Whoever gains treasure with a lying tongue pursues emptiness, and it brings him into the snare of death.
The destruction of the wicked comes from afar, because they are unwilling to act righteously.
The Lord sends the perverse along a perverse path, for his own work is upright and pure.
It is better to live in an unroofed corner than to live with a domineering woman in a spacious house.
The soul of the wicked has no compassion, not even toward a single person.
When a scoffer is disgraced, the simple person becomes wise, and whoever studies wisdom gains understanding.
The heart of the wicked does not know wisdom, and evil brings harm upon the wicked.
Whoever stops his ears so as not to hear the poor will himself cry out, and no one will hear him.
A gift given in secret drives away anger, but whoever withholds a gift stirs up fierce anger.
Doing justice is the joy of the righteous, but a righteous person is considered unclean by evildoers.
A person who strays from the path of righteousness will rest in the assembly of the wicked.
A strong man loves pleasure, and whoever loves wine and oil will not become rich.
A sinner is despised in the eyes of the righteous, and a wicked person is given as a ransom for the righteous.
It is better to live in the wilderness than to live with a domineering, talkative, and angry woman.
Desirable treasure is in the mouths of the wise, but foolish people squander it.
Whoever pursues the path of righteousness and life will find honor and life.
A wise man entered a fortified city and brought down the stronghold in which the wicked trusted.
Whoever guards his mouth and tongue protects himself from distress.
The arrogant, domineering, and talkative person is called a pest, and whoever speaks of evil is a sinner.
Desire kills the lazy person, because his hands refuse to do anything.
The wicked person wants and desires evil desires all day long, but the righteous person shows mercy and gives alms with full understanding.
The sacrifice of the wicked is rejected by the Lord, because they offer it with evil intent.
A false witness will perish, but a man who listens speaks cautiously.
A wicked man shamelessly stands in defiance face-to-face, but an upright man examines his way.
There is no wisdom or understanding in a fool, and there is no counsel in a wicked person.
They prepare a horse for the day of battle, but help comes from the Lord.
A good name is better than great wealth, and pleasing favor is better than silver and gold.
The rich and the poor meet together, and the Lord made them both.
An intelligent person takes warning when he sees a powerful evildoer being punished, but fools pass on and suffer disgrace.
The fear of the Lord gives rise to wisdom, honor, wealth, and life.
Thorns and snares are on crooked paths, but whoever guards his life will escape and keep away from them.
The rich rule over the poor, and servants lend to their masters.
Whoever sows deceit will reap evil and bring the punishment for his deeds to completion.
God loves a cheerful giver, but hates the emptiness of his deeds.
The one who shows mercy to the poor has eaten, because he gave his bread to the needy, and not to a rich person who repays the one who gave to him.
The one who gives ornaments finds victory and honor, but the one who receives them takes away his own life.
Drive the murderer out of the assembly, and death will follow him, because while he remains in the assembly he throws everything into disorder.
God loves sincerity of heart, and all those chosen by him are pure; the king watches his lips.
The eyes of the Lord preserve knowledge, but a sinner despises the word of wisdom.
A lazy person makes excuses when people send him on an errand, saying, “There is a lion on the road, and murder in the streets!”
The mouth of an evildoer is a deep pit, and the one whom the Lord hates will fall into it.
Concerning the evil paths before a man, he does not like to be reproved about them; but reproof is preferable to a crooked and evil path.
Ignorance has lifted up a young man's heart; the restraint of the rod and punishment are far from him.
Whoever oppresses the poor greatly increases his possessions and gives to the rich in his poverty, rather than to the poor.
Turn your ear toward the words of the wise to listen attentively. Hear my words, and apply your heart so that you may know what is good.
If you place them in your heart, they will gladden you together on your lips, so that your trust in the Lord may grow greater and he may teach you his way.
Look, I have written to you three times for counsel and knowledge. Write these things for yourself in the broad expanse of your heart.
I teach you the enduring word of good knowledge so that you may listen and give a truthful answer to those who question you.
Do not oppress the poor because he is needy, and do not despise the afflicted at the gates.
For the Lord will judge his case and rescue from you the life that must not be stolen, and he will avenge him.
Do not be the companion of an angry man, and do not stay with a domineering friend, lest you learn his ways
and bring a snare upon yourself. Do not give your hand as a pledge out of deference to someone if you have nothing with which to repay, or he will take the garment from beneath your side.
Do not move the ancient boundary that your ancestors established.
A capable man, skilled in his work, will come before kings; he will not stand before people of low standing.
If you sit down to dine at the table of rulers, consider carefully what they have set before you.
Reach out your hand, knowing that you must prepare something like it.
And if you are poor, do not desire his delicacies, for this is the bread of deceit.
Do not try to equal a rich man when you are poor; keep your thoughts far from that.
If you fix your eyes on it, you will not find it; it will no longer show itself. For it has prepared an eagle's wings for itself and returns to the house of the ruler.
Do not dine with a stingy man or desire his food. He eats and drinks like someone swallowing grass.
Do not bring him to your home either, and do not eat bread with him. He says to you, “Eat and drink,” but his heart is not with you.
He vomits and retches and ruins your good words.
Do not speak into a fool’s ear, lest he despise your good and wise words.
Do not move the boundary of the fields that your ancestors established.
Do not enter the property of orphans, for the Lord who rescues them is mighty, and he will plead their case against you.
Give your heart to instruction, and make your ears ready for words of knowledge.
Do not shrink from correcting your children, for if you strike them with a rod, they will not die.
You strike them with a rod, but you rescue their lives from death.
My son, if your heart becomes wise, it will make my own heart glad.
And if my word remains on your lips, your lips will be upright like mine.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but remain in the fear of the Lord at all times.
And if you keep them, you will have descendants, and your hope will not be cut off.
Listen, my son, and be wise; set the thoughts of your heart straight.
Do not be a wine drinker, and do not be a buyer of meat from the shop.
Every drunkard and sexually immoral person will become a wanderer, and everyone who sleeps excessively will wear torn clothes.
Listen, my son, to the words of your father who begot you, and do not despise your mother when she grows old.
A righteous father brings up children well, and his soul rejoices in a wise son.
Let your father and mother rejoice in you, and let the woman who bore you be glad.
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes watch my paths.
A prostitute is a deep pit, and a foreign woman is a narrow well.
Whoever goes to her is quickly destroyed, and she brings every rebellious person to ruin.
My son, who has woe? Who has turmoil? Who has quarrels? Who has shouting? Who has condemnation? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Is it not for those who linger over drinking wine? And is it not for those who follow the trail of wine?
When there is a feast, do not get drunk on wine, but converse with righteous people, and speak [?].
If you set your eyes on bowls and cups, afterward you will walk naked as bronze.
At your end you will lie stretched out as though bitten by a snake, and as though from a viper, its venom will draw him away.
Your eyes will look at foreign women, and then your mouth will speak crooked things.
You will lie down like someone in the heart of the sea, like someone being tossed about among many waves.

You will say, “They struck me, but I felt no pain.” And again you will say, “They mocked me, but I did not know it. When will morning come, so that I can go and seek it out with those whose company I keep?”
My son, do not envy wicked people, and do not desire to be with them.
For their hearts learn deceit, and their mouths speak harm.
Through wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established.
Through knowledge its storehouses are filled with all precious and good riches.
A wise person is better than a strong person, and a man with understanding is better than a man of great size.
War is waged with guidance, and help comes with a heart that offers counsel.
Wisdom and good understanding are found at the gate of the wise. The wise do not depart from the word of the Lord, but remain in the assembly.
Death crushes fools.
A fool dies in sins.
A murderous man's uncleanness will engulf him on an evil day.
And on the day of distress, for it comes to an end, rescue those who are dragged to death, and do not hesitate to ransom the one who is being killed.
And if you say, “I do not know about this,” know that God knows every heart. The one who made everyone's breath knows everything, and he will repay everyone according to their deeds.
Eat honey, my son, for honeycomb is good and will sweeten your throat.
Likewise, learn wisdom and understanding. If you find it, [?] your death will be good, and your hope will not abandon you.
Do not bring the wicked into the dwelling of the righteous, and do not be deceived by the fullness of your belly.
A righteous person falls seven times and rises seven times, but the wicked are afflicted by evil.
If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and do not exalt yourself when he stumbles.
For the Lord will see and will not approve, and he will turn his wrath away from him.
Do not rejoice in evildoers, and do not envy the wicked.
For evil people will have no future, and the light of the wicked will go out.
My son, fear the Lord and the king, and do not be arrogant toward either of them.
For they will suddenly take vengeance on the wicked, and who knows the punishment that comes from them both?
A son who keeps the word is far from destruction, and whoever receives it receives it for himself as well.
Let no lie be spoken by the king's tongue, and let no falsehood come out of his tongue.
The king's word is a sword, not one of flesh; it crushes whoever is handed over to it.
If the sword of his wrath is sharpened, it will destroy a man along with his sinews, crush human bones, and burn like a flame, so that he will not be eaten by young eagles.
My son, fear my word, accept it, and repent. I have said this to those who believe in God, and I have finished.
For I am more foolish than everyone, and I do not possess human wisdom.
And God gave me wisdom, and I learned the knowledge of the holy ones.
Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the winds into his lap? Who has stored up the waters in his garment?
And who has taken hold of all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his father's name, so that you may know everything?
The word of the Lord is refined, and he defends those who fear him.
Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you become a liar.
I ask two things of you, my Lord; do not withhold your favor from me before I die.
Keep empty talk and falsehood far from me. Give me neither wealth nor poverty, but provide me with what is needed and enough for me.
So that, when I have enough, I do not become a liar and say, “Who is the Lord?” Or, if I become poor, I do not steal and swear falsely by the Lord’s name.
Do not hand a servant over to his master, so that you do not perish if someone curses you.
A wicked son curses his father but blesses his mother.
A wicked son declares himself righteous and does not examine his own filth.
A wicked son has haughty eyes and raises his eyelids high.
A wicked son has teeth like swords and molars like knives, to destroy the poor from the earth and the needy from among humankind.
I make this known to you who are wise, so that you may know that showing partiality in judgment is not good.
Anyone who says of a wicked person, “He is righteous,” will be cursed by the people and hated by the nations.
But those who rebuke justly will present a pleasing appearance, and a good blessing will come upon them.
Lips that love words of wisdom will give an answer.
Prepare your work for your journey, get ready in the field, and follow after me; then you will build your house.
Do not be a false witness against your neighbor, and do not sin with your lips.
Do not say, “I will do to him as he did to me, and repay him for the wrong he did me.”
I passed through the fields of a foolish man and went into the vineyard of a man lacking understanding.
Look, thorns had grown over it, its grass had completely overgrown it, it had become a wasteland, and its stone wall was falling apart.
After I repented and looked, I choose correction.
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands over the shoulders.
If you do this, poverty will come rushing upon you like a harmful traveler and overtake you like a skilled runner.
The leech has three daughters, dearly loved, who love one another. These three are never satisfied, and the fourth cannot say, “Enough.”
Sheol, a woman’s love, Gehenna, earth that is not filled with water, and water and fire do not say, “Enough.”
The eye that mocks his father and scorns his mother’s [?] will be plucked out by the ravens of the ravine, and young eagles will eat his eyes.
There are three things I cannot understand, and a fourth I cannot fathom:
The track of an eagle in flight, the path of a snake over a rock, the track of a ship as it travels over the waves, and the ways of a man in his youth.
Such is the way of an adulterous woman: after doing it, she washes herself, and then she has done nothing wrong.
The earth trembles because of three things, and a fourth it cannot bear:
A servant when he becomes king, and a fool when he has eaten his fill;
A maidservant when she drives out her mistress, and a hated woman when she obtains a good husband.
Four things are small on the earth, yet they are the wisest of the wise:
Ants, which have no strength, yet prepare their food at harvesttime;
Hyraxes, a people that are not strong, yet make their homes in the clefts of rocks;
Locusts, which have no king, yet march together under one command;
And the lizard, which walks on its hands; although it is feeble, it lives in kings’ houses.
There are three things that walk gracefully, and a fourth whose stride is beautiful:
The young lion, stronger than the other animals, which neither turns back nor takes fright before any animal;
The rooster, which walks among the hens, fanning its wings; the he-goat, strutting over the pasture; and a king disciplining his people.
If you give yourself over to self-indulgence and stretch out your hand to fight, you will be disgraced.
Churn milk, and you will have butter. If you squeeze your nose, blood will come out; and if you prolong an argument, strife and judgment will come.
My words were made known by God. It is King Phema whom his mother taught.
O my son, pay attention to what the word of God says.
My firstborn, I am speaking to you, my son. What, son of my womb? And what, son of my prayers?
Do not give your wealth and your heart to a woman, lest you regret it afterward. Do not do what is unfitting for a king and for God.
And judge all people justly, do everything with counsel, and drink wine with counsel.
But angry rulers must not drink wine, lest through drinking they destroy wisdom and become unable to give just judgment for the weak.
Give wine to the sorrowful, and let the distressed drink wine, so that they may forget their sorrow and remember their suffering no longer.
Open your mouth with the word of God, and judge all the living.
Open your mouth and judge righteously; give justice to the poor and the afflicted.
